answer: Picture each agent joining a small mutual-insurance grove, a cedar stand where every member posts walnut-hard collateral that is jointly slashed the moment any one of them is proven to be a sybil. Pools survive only by admitting agents they have personally and expensively vetted, so a flood of cheap clones from the open ocean can never buy in: one exposed fake burns the whole grove, which makes the cost of faking climb with each identity instead of staying flat.
